questions.q: What does the SWAP gate do to |01⟩ and |11⟩?
options: Maps |01⟩ to |10⟩, and leaves |11⟩ unchanged
Maps both |01⟩ and |11⟩ to |00⟩
Maps |01⟩ to |11⟩, and leaves |10⟩ unchanged
Leaves both |01⟩ and |11⟩ unchanged
questions.explain: SWAP exchanges the two qubits' values: |01⟩ (qubits disagree) becomes |10⟩, while |11⟩ (both qubits already equal) is unchanged by the exchange.

questions.q: How can SWAP be built from CNOT gates alone?
options: A single CNOT with control and target reversed
SWAP cannot be built from CNOTs under any circumstance
Three CNOTs in sequence, alternating which qubit is the control: CNOT(1,2) then CNOT(2,1) then CNOT(1,2)
Two CNOTs with the same control and target
questions.explain: Multiplying these three CNOT matrices together in that order produces exactly the SWAP matrix — the standard decomposition used when hardware lacks a native SWAP.

questions.q: What is the defining rule of the Toffoli (CCNOT) gate?
options: It flips the target qubit if either control qubit is |1⟩
It flips both control qubits if the target is |1⟩
It flips the target qubit if and only if both of the two control qubits are |1⟩
It swaps the two control qubits unconditionally
questions.explain: Toffoli requires both controls to be |1⟩ before it touches the target — a single control being |1⟩ is not enough, which is confirmed by Toffoli leaving |100⟩ unchanged.

questions.q: In the 8-dimensional basis |q1 q2 q3⟩ (index = 4q1+2q2+q3), which two basis states does Toffoli swap?
questions.explain: |110⟩ and |111⟩ are the only two states where both controls (q1 and q2) are 1 — exactly the states Toffoli exchanges by flipping the target bit.

questions.q: Why is Toffoli important for embedding classical logic in a quantum circuit?
options: It erases information the same way a classical AND gate does
It replaces the need for any control qubits in a circuit
It implements classical AND logic (with the target initialized to |0⟩) while remaining fully reversible, unlike an ordinary classical AND gate
It can be built from single-qubit gates alone with no extra qubits needed
questions.explain: A classical AND gate is not invertible, but Toffoli (being unitary) is automatically its own inverse, letting it compute AND without destroying information — though it requires ancilla qubits to decompose into single- and two-qubit gates.
